subject: Compiler Design
question: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding LR parsers?
options: A. LALR(1) parser can have shift-reduce conflicts that are not present in CLR(1)
B. LALR(1) parser can have reduce-reduce conflicts that are not present in CLR(1)
C. SLR(1) parser has strictly more states than LALR(1) parser
D. LR(0) parser can parse all LL(1) grammars
explanation: LALR(1) is constructed by merging states of CLR(1) that have identical sets of core items. Merging states with identical cores never produces shift-reduce conflicts, but it CAN produce reduce-reduce conflicts if lookaheads overlap.

subject: Compiler Design
question: An SDD is S-attributed if every attribute is synthesized. Which of the following is true for L-attributed definitions?
options: A. Inherited attributes of a symbol can depend on right sibling attributes
B. Inherited attributes of a symbol can depend only on parent and left sibling attributes
C. It cannot be evaluated in a single depth-first left-to-right pass
D. It cannot contain synthesized attributes
explanation: In an L-attributed SDD, each inherited attribute of node X_j in production A -> X_1 X_2 ... X_n can depend only on inherited attributes of parent A and attributes of symbols X_1 ... X_{j-1} to its left.
